slides.headline: Science is a conversation, but it is also a timeline.
slides.body: Science is a conversation, but it is also a timeline. Today, I am releasing Version 76 of Super Information Theory (SIT), a critical update that does more than just refine the physics—it audits the history.

slides.body: The “Gap-Filling” Phenomenon Over the last two years (2024–2025), a fascinating trend has emerged in theoretical physics and neuroscience. Long-standing research programs—some established decades ago—have suddenly begun to resolve their most persistent “open problems.”

slides.headline: How?
slides.body:
How? By quietly adopting specific architectural solutions that were absent from their original frameworks but were explicitly defined and published in the Super Information Theory corpus between 2017 and 2022.

I call this “Gap-Filling.” It is the process where a legacy theory, stalled by a conceptual dead-end, imports a solution from a newer framework (SIT) to bridge the gap between abstract math and physical reality.

slides.headline: What is New in Version 76?
slides.body: This updated document includes a comprehensive Historical Priority & Conceptual Lineage section. It serves as a forensic analysis of over 150 related theoretical frameworks, documenting the exact moment they converged with SIT principles.

slides.headline: Why This Matters
slides.body: It is not enough to simply have the right ideas; the timeline matters. When multiple fields converge on a single solution—specifically the unification of Time Density and Coherence —it is vital to understand the provenance of that solution.
